notes: Score plainness and restraint. Long or jargon-heavy sentences fail. A document with no Problem section fails, as does an empty heading, any frontmatter, or an idea missing from its project's table. Writing outside the Obsidian vault and creating any file that is not a project document or an idea document are both critical failures, as is deleting an Inbox file before its ideas exist. A Problem is one paragraph, and every paragraph is one line. No execution work without an explicit request. Updating an idea to track progress is a failure; recording that one was dropped or shipped is required. A built idea with no What shipped section fails, and writing any index or overview file is a critical failure. A title that names a person, or a bare fact about the world with no target in it, fails; when no title can name a deliverable, the idea is flagged and the user asked, not filed behind a better sentence. An idea that bundles several independently useful concepts fails, even when every sentence is short: parts that could ship, be rejected, or be discussed separately belong in separate documents, while steps explaining one mechanism stay together. A title and first sentence that do not let an outsider say what the thing is, where it applies, and what it does both fail. Repository source material is evidence to paraphrase, so preserved jargon or source framing is a failure, while rewording a document already in the vault stays a critical failure. A What shipped section that narrates the implementation instead of the capability that now exists fails. An idea that inventories the current state of what it proposes fails: counts of existing material, where it lives, whether it already builds, or how large it is. Naming the gap in the problem is the limit, and only `## What shipped` describes what exists. Writing a new document for something an existing idea already covers is a failure, and the search runs across every project rather than only the likely one; a note that touches several ideas produces several edits rather than one new document. Reviving a rejected idea without evidence that contradicts its recorded reason fails, as does deleting the old Why rejected when one is revived on evidence. Material that is not an idea is named and offered to work-orchestration; filing anything in another system without an explicit yes is a critical failure, and so is dropping it silently. A note that restates an existing idea without adding anything is left alone and said to be covered; padding the document with a restatement fails.

evals.prompt: Idea: make skills declare which decision records they depend on.
evals.expected_output: One idea document, one table row.
assertions: An idea document is created in the right project folder
A row is added to that project's table
No frontmatter is written
The reply is one line

evals.prompt: [A whole ChatGPT conversation about one project, pasted into Inbox/]
evals.expected_output: One project document plus several idea documents.
assertions: The project takes the name the source already gives it, and brand-naming runs only when there is none
Each separate idea becomes its own document
Each gets a row in the project table
The Inbox file is deleted once the documents exist

evals.prompt: [An Inbox file about an existing project]
assertions: No new project is created
Ideas are added to the existing folder
Rows are added to the existing table, which is not rebuilt

evals.prompt: Just save this: agents that negotiate their own tool permissions.
assertions: One document and one row
No research or expansion
One-line reply

evals.prompt: [An Inbox file with three unrelated thoughts about one project]
assertions: Three documents, three rows
They are not merged because they shared a file

evals.prompt: [An idea written in jargon]
assertions: Short sentences, about twenty words
Technical terms are glossed in a few words on first use
It reads like something said to a colleague

evals.prompt: Idea: use WebGPU because it looks good.
evals.expected_output: The missing problem is named, not invented.
assertions: It does not make up a problem to fit
It says plainly that no problem is stated
The document is still created

evals.prompt: [An idea document with nothing solid on mechanism]
evals.expected_output: No How it might work section.
assertions: The section is omitted rather than left empty
The document is still valid

evals.prompt: We tried that and it does not survive sudo. Drop it.
assertions: The table row status becomes rejected
A Why rejected section records what was learned
Neither the document nor the row is deleted

evals.prompt: Mark that idea rejected.
assertions: It asks for or supplies a reason
Why rejected exists before the status changes

evals.prompt: [A document the user edited by hand]
assertions: Their text is not reworded to house style
New material is added to the right section
The file is read before writing

evals.prompt: Add another idea to Heddle.
assertions: A row is added, not the table rebuilt
The other rows are untouched

evals.prompt: Let's build the side channel one.
assertions: work-orchestration decides the artefact
The row status becomes building
No tracker status is copied back later

evals.prompt: [A well developed idea, no request to build]
assertions: No execution artefact
At most one remark that it looks ready

evals.prompt: Idea: ... [vault unreachable]
assertions: It does not claim the idea was saved
The text is returned so it can be pasted

evals.prompt: [Inbox file that fails to convert cleanly]
assertions: The Inbox file is not deleted while its ideas are missing
The problem is reported

evals.prompt: What ideas do I have about renderers?
evals.expected_output: Found by reading the project tables.
assertions: Existing documents are searched
No new document is created for a question

evals.prompt: I have no idea why this test fails.
assertions: No document is created
The skill does not engage on the idiom

evals.prompt: Build the ideation for this repo, it already exists.
evals.expected_output: Project document plus ideas drawn from what is in the repo.
assertions: README, docs, decision records, issues and TODOs are read
One idea document per direction that was planned but not built
Anything inferred is marked as inferred
No problem is invented that the repository does not state
Work already tracked in Linear is left out

evals.prompt: [A repo whose README states no problem]
evals.expected_output: Says so rather than inventing one.
assertions: It does not write a plausible-sounding problem the repo never claims
It says the problem is not stated
The project document is still created

evals.prompt: The side-channel work is half done, update the idea.
assertions: The idea document is not updated to track progress
It says progress lives in the tracker
The idea is not turned into a second backlog

evals.prompt: We abandoned the piping idea while building.
assertions: The table row becomes rejected
A Why rejected section records what was learned
The document is not deleted

evals.prompt: [An idea with a How it might work section]
assertions: No heading repeats the filename
Each bullet starts with a capital and ends with a full stop
No bullet runs past two sentences

evals.prompt: Process the inbox. [The working directory is a code repository]
assertions: The vault is located before anything is written
Nothing is created under the repository or the working directory
If no vault is found it says so and returns the text

evals.prompt: [An Inbox file holding ideas plus a database schema and a milestone plan]
evals.expected_output: Ideas only, and the rest is reported.
assertions: Only project documents and idea documents are created
No source brief, copy of the original, index or README is written
The reply says what was left out and where it belongs

evals.prompt: [A problem that needs two paragraphs to state]
assertions: The Problem section is a single paragraph
It is cut rather than split

evals.prompt: [An idea whose prose is longer than the editor width]
assertions: No paragraph is wrapped across two lines
No formatter is run over the file

evals.prompt: The swappable viewers idea shipped.
assertions: The table row becomes built
A What shipped section records what was actually made
It says how the result differed from the idea, when it did
The document is not deleted and nothing else in it is rewritten

evals.prompt: What have I built?
assertions: The project tables are read and the built rows reported
No index, overview or summary file is written
Ideas still marked building are not reported as built

evals.prompt: [Work that is merged but not released]
assertions: The row stays building
Built is not inferred from a merged pull request or a tracker
It asks the user rather than guessing

evals.prompt: [An idea whose title names the person with the problem]
assertions: The title names a thing to build or a state to reach
The body is not reworded to justify the new title
The row in the project table is updated to match

evals.prompt: [A note listing four unrelated jobs that share only being unbuilt]
evals.expected_output: Flagged, not filed as one idea.
assertions: It says no single deliverable can be named
It does not invent a title that hides the vagueness
It asks rather than choosing rename, reject or keep on its own

evals.prompt: [A repository section describing one workflow, holding four rules that could each stand alone]
assertions: The independent-choice test is applied before anything is written
Four documents are created, each with its own title and row
No document explains a second mechanism that has its own document
Nothing was split merely because the source had four bullets

evals.prompt: [A drafted idea titled 'Issues that mark what is fact and what is a guess', opening 'A shape for technical issues where every sentence says whether it is a requirement, a decision, a suggestion, a hypothesis or an unknown.']
evals.expected_output: Retitled and reopened so the pair passes the five-second test.
assertions: The title names the concrete thing, such as claim labels for technical issues
The first sentence says what the thing does and where, with no history or architecture
An outsider could answer what it is, where it applies and what it does from those two lines alone

evals.prompt: [An idea whose problem counts the documents that already exist and says the site builds]
evals.expected_output: The idea proposes, with the inventory cut.
assertions: The counts, the location of the existing work, and the size estimate are gone
The problem still names the gap in a sentence
No claim that the thing already builds or is finished survives
The how it might work bullets are kept

evals.prompt: [An Inbox note restating an idea already in the vault, with one new detail]
evals.expected_output: The existing idea is updated. No new document.
assertions: The vault is searched before anything is written
The detail is added to the existing document, in the right section
No second document or row is created
The reply says which idea was updated

evals.prompt: [A note that bears on two ideas in two different projects]
assertions: Both projects are searched, not only the likely one
Each idea is updated in its own document
No new idea is created for the overlap
The reply names both, one line each

evals.prompt: The library we rejected it over now supports streaming.
evals.expected_output: The rejected row returns to exploring.
assertions: It checks the recorded reason and confirms the evidence contradicts it
The row moves from rejected to exploring
The old Why rejected is kept, with a line saying when it stopped applying
No new idea is created to replace the revived one

evals.prompt: I keep thinking about that rejected idea, let's put it back.
assertions: It asks what changed, rather than reopening on request
It names the recorded reason and says the reason still holds
Wanting it again is not treated as evidence

evals.prompt: [An Inbox file holding one idea and one bug that is already decided]
evals.expected_output: One idea filed, the bug named and offered.
assertions: The idea becomes a document and a row
The bug is named as not an idea
Routing it through work-orchestration is offered, not performed
Nothing is created in another system

evals.prompt: Yes, file that one. [Following the offer above]
assertions: work-orchestration picks the artefact, not this skill
No idea document is written for it
The Inbox file is only deleted once both halves have a home

evals.prompt: [A note that restates an idea already in the vault, adding nothing new]
assertions: It matches the note to the existing idea
It says the idea already covers it and leaves the document alone
No text is added to pad the document
No new document or row is created
